Fatties always tend to use it as an excuse to be fat, and I see a lot of people saying "I know someone that has a thyroid problem and she eats so healthy and goes to the gym and she's still big because of her thyroid." Personally I feel like this is a big load of shit but I wanted to get a second opinion. How does having a thyroid problem affect you in terms of weight? If you are a bit big but apparently eat healthy and exercise, is it really your thyroid doing this or is it possibly your diet, amount of exercise, etc. Also, how much harder is it to lose weight when you have a thyroid problem? I read this to look into it but wanted to get a second opinion on the matter. I just feel like it's unlikely that you stay a bit larger when you have a thyroid problem, considering people such as Jillian Michaels who has one and is fit as hell, but I just wanted to double check. Thanks.

Well, it does make it a bit easier to gain weight, and somewhat harder to lose it, but once you start taking the supplemental hormones, you're pretty much back to normal. Before getting my diagnosis, I needed to keep an eye on my intake, or I'd put on about 10lb over a 6-12 months, but then I'd stabilize there. Getting back down again required discipline and, I felt at the time, a disproportionally large cut in intake, at least compared to most people I know.

Once I was diagnosed and put on supplemental hormones, I started losing weight without having made any changes in my intake (or exercise), and lost about 6lb. At that point my weight loss had pretty much stopped, but it's possible it would have continued for a little bit further if I hadn't allowed my intake to increase a bit. According to the dietitian I was remitted to, I'd been eating a bit less that what her calculations said a person like me ought to in order to maintain a stable weight, so she suggested I try eating a bit more. When I did, the weight loss ceased, and I eventually stabilized at about 5lb below my previous target weight.

Whenever I hear about doughnut snorters claiming "thyroid problems" as the cause of their morbid obesity, I tend to jump to the conclusion that it is a) self-diagnosed, b) untreated, and c) bullshit. You can lose weight even if you do have hypothyroidism and refuse to treat it with supplemental hormones - sure, it'll be a bit more effort than if you took your damn medicine, but, as always with overweight, just a matter of discipline, since your thyroid, broken or not, does not have the ability to violate the laws of thermodynamics, nor does it take over your brain and force you to stuff yourself with fried food and chocolate.

However, if you actually have the diagnosed the condition, why the hell wouldn't you take the pill to correct it? And once you do take the pill, the majority of the effects it has on you - including the issues not related to your cake hole - will go away, and no longer impact you in any major way.

I guess the effects, and response to the medication, varies, and that there are some people for whom the effects are more severe, and/or the medication less effective, but not only is this rare, but even when it occurs, it only makes it a bit harder to lose/maintain your weight, not impossible.
